name: Passive Voice
moduleIntroduction: Welcome to the Passive Voice module! This is how we translate the French word 'On'. In English, we often shift the focus from *who* did the action to *what* happened. If you don't master this, you will struggle to say things like 'On m'a dit' or 'On a volé mon sac'.
contrastiveExplanation:
The 'On' Problem:
English: No word for 'On'. We use Passive Voice. (On a réparé la route -> The road was repaired).
French: Uses Active voice with 'On'.

Structure:
English: Be + Past Participle (is done, was eaten).
French: Être + Participe Passé (est fait). *Warning: Students often forget the 'Be' in English.*

Indirect Objects:
English: You can start with the person. (I was told).
French: You cannot. (On m'a dit -> Il m'a été dit is rare/formal).

commonErrors.frenchConnection: Translating 'On m'a dit' literally. Use the passive voice.
Forgetting the verb 'to be'. A past participle cannot be the main verb alone.
Over-using passive. Verbs with no object (happen, die, arrive) cannot be passive.
French uses 'Je suis né' (Present auxiliary). English uses 'Was born' (Past).

commonErrors.correct: The rule was explained to me.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Some verbs (explain) cannot make the person the subject in passive.

items.feedback: Correct! Present Simple Passive (It is done).
Correct! Past Simple Passive (It was done).
Correct! Rice doesn't grow itself; people grow it.
Correct! Language is spoken by people.

items.questionText: The food ___ cooked by my mother.
Football ___ played all over the world.
This song ___ sung by a famous artist.

items.feedback: Correct! Present Continuous Passive (Is being done).
Correct! Present Perfect Passive (Have been + PP).
Correct! Standard passive 'was arrested'. ('Got' is informal but 'was' is standard).

items.questionText: The cake ___ eaten by the dog.

items.feedback: Correct! 'Need' + -ing has a passive meaning (needs to be cleaned).

items.questionText: Translate: "On m'a dit que tu étais là."
options: I was told that you were here.
items.correctAnswer: I was told that you were here.

items.questionText: He ___ a job at the bank.
items.feedback: Correct! 'On lui a offert' -> 'He was offered'.

items.questionText: Find the error: "The accident was happened yesterday."
items.feedback: Correct! 'Happen' is intransitive. It CANNOT be passive. Say 'The accident happened'.

items.questionText: It is ___ that he is rich.
She ___ to be the best singer.

items.feedback: Correct! 'Get' passive is common in informal English.

items.questionText: Find the error: "I was explained the lesson."
items.feedback: Correct! You cannot say 'I was explained'. You must say 'The lesson was explained to me'.
items.correction: The lesson was explained to me

items.feedback: Correct! 'Remain' is intransitive. Cannot be passive.
Correct! Passive of 'Make' takes 'to'. (Active: Made him pay. Passive: Was made TO pay).

items.questionText: He dislikes ___ told what to do.
It is ___ that the economy will grow.
items.feedback: Correct! 'It is believed that...' (On croit que).
Correct! 'See' in passive takes -ing or 'to' (to enter). -ing implies continuous.

items.questionText: The book ___ written by Chinua Achebe.
The window ___ broken by the ball.
Find the error: "The event was occurred yesterday."
items.feedback: Correct! 'Occur' is intransitive. Say 'The event occurred'.

items.questionText: It is ___ that he is guilty.
Find the error: "He was suggested a new plan."
items.feedback: Correct! 'Suggest' cannot have a person subject in passive. Say 'A plan was suggested to him'.
items.correction: A new plan was suggested to him

items.questionText: She is known ___ a good doctor.
It is ___ that prices will rise.
